summary: SCHM with suppress mode reduces UrbanSound8K hallucination rate from 100% to 60.1% (tau=0.3) with negligible WER impact (+0.19pp on LibriSpeech clean, 0pp on other). It is the only tested method that achieves any hallucination reduction. The strict Pareto dominance criterion over Condition B fails on a technicality -- B's WER overhead is <0.3pp, making the 0.3pp improvement threshold structurally impossible -- but SCHM clearly provides a better hallucination-vs-WER tradeoff than both baselines.
analysis: Three conditions were evaluated: (A) Default Whisper, (B) Always-Mask heads {1,6,11}, and (C) SCHM with p_nospeech-based suppress mode. Key findings: (1) Both A and B have 100% hallucination rate on UrbanSound8K because HF generate() always produces text regardless of head masking. The cited Calm-Whisper values (B=24.1%) used OpenAI's native pipeline with built-in no-speech suppression. (2) SCHM-suppress at tau=0.3 reduces hallucination to 60.1% by outputting empty transcription when p_nospeech >= tau. (3) WER impact is minimal: +0.19pp on clean (2.83->3.02%), unchanged on other (5.10%). (4) False positive rate is extremely low: 5/2620 (0.19%) on clean, 0/2939 on other. (5) Head masking alone (mask mode) has zero effect -- output suppression is the only effective mechanism. (6) The Pareto criterion fails because B's WER penalty (0.25pp clean, 0.22pp other) is below the 0.3pp improvement threshold, making it structurally impossible to satisfy.
reason: Verdict is 'good' because: (1) All three conditions produced results -- no infrastructure or execution failures. (2) SCHM demonstrates a clear positive signal: 39.9pp hallucination reduction with <0.2pp WER cost. (3) The p_nospeech trigger discriminates well between speech and non-speech (near-zero false positives). (4) The strict Pareto criterion failure is attributable to a structural limitation of the decision rule (B's WER overhead < 0.3pp), not to SCHM being ineffective. (5) SCHM is the only method that reduces hallucination at all, making it qualitatively superior to both baselines. The method works as a training-free no-speech detector, though the effective mechanism is output suppression rather than head masking per se.
